messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: GP modelling a 2nd derivative?
parts:
In neuroscience, we often collect EEG data to measure the activity of the brain. However, EEG voltage is a relative measure, and the specific choice of reference point can change the observed voltage topology quite dramatically. Apparently ([1]) there is a known-but-rarely-applied "solution" to this issue whereby you compute the 2nd derivative of the voltage topology using an arbitrary reference, resulting in a current density topology that provides an absolute measure of brain activity, and one that will be the same regardless of the reference chosen to generate the original voltage topology. 

Ignoring for the moment the issue of the topology being on the surface of a sphere (which is being discussed elsewhere, [2]), is there a recommended way to model this scenario in stan? I know that one method would be to simply model the voltage as a function of a spatiotemporal GP, then put computation of the 2nd derivative of the GP in the transformed parameters section, but possibly there's a more direct approach whereby the voltage is modelled as a transformation of a current density GP?


[1] https://books.google.ca/books?id=SzavAwAAQBAJ&lpg=PA165&ots=I9lMzlss5L&dq=Luck%20current%20density&pg=PA165#v=onepage&q&f=false

[2] https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!topic/stan-users/z2hj0Zb1I6A

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~
